name: L'Hombre
description: L'Hombre (Spanish for 'The Man') is a historical three-player card game that was the most popular and prestigious card game in Europe for over two centuries (c. 1650-1850). Played with a 40-card Spanish-suited (or standard) deck, it introduced the revolutionary concept of bidding to determine the trump suit and the 'declarer' (The Hombre) who plays alone against the other two. It is the direct ancestor of games like Ombre, Quadrille, and Skat.

content.text: L'Hombre (Spanish for 'The Man') is a historical three-player card game that was the most popular and prestigious card game in Europe for over two centuries (c. 1650-1850). Played with a 40-card Spanish-suited (or standard) deck, it introduced the revolutionary concept of bidding to determine the trump suit and the 'declarer' (The Hombre) who plays alone against the other two. It is the direct ancestor of games like Ombre, Quadrille, and Skat.
Developed in Spain in the early 17th century. It was a courtly game, widely mentioned in classical literature (e.g., Cervantes, Pope).
3 players (The Hombre plays against the other two).
40 cards. 8s, 9s, 10s removed. Rank (Non-trump): K, Q, J, 7-2, A (in black suits) or 2-4, K, Q, J, A (in red suits).

Each player receives 9 cards. 13 cards form a talon (Pila).

items.text: Grand: Only Spadille and Basta count as trumps. Both declarer and defenders exchange with the talon. Declarer must exchange at least five cards; win requires at least five tricks. Rated like Grand Tourné or Simple Nolo.
Grandissimo: Like Grand but declarer does not exchange any cards; to Grand what Solo is to Simple Game.

Bonus for first five tricks: Declarer may declare intent to take the first five tricks before playing to the first trick. Success scores an extra token; failure loses one token to each player. Outcome is independent of the contract result.
